So, If I understand my physics correctly, it doesn't matter how wide your tires are. For every extra square inch of rubber you add you also reduce the amount of weight each square inch supports. Ergo, wider tires wouldn't necessarily give you better traction...so what's with the huge wide racing tires?
Softer rubber grips with less pressure, as better compounds come into use optimum tire size goes up. Tires are not always under optimum load, larger tires allow for more consistent grip.

The contact patch size generally fails for rigid objects, which tires are not. Think of the tire surface being deformed by the miniscule hills and valleys of the pavement and how the rubber would have to flow around them to skid. The wider tire would have fewer deformations per square inch, and what deformations were present wouldn't be as deep, but the effort to move the rubber around them isn't linear.

Downforce increases the effective weight of the car as the speed goes up so it gets more grip from the extra width. This is why F1 cars have to be driven flat out to actually get any grip - they warm the tyres and add downforce as the speed goes up.

If it satisfies you, there might be the sound of a creek, if a creek is nearby. All other sound, when entering the sanctum, will be reduced to silence.
